title: Best of Bhutan FREE Visit to Taktsang Monastery
highlights: Experience the magic of Bhutan as you journey through Paro’s lush green valleys, Thimphu’s exquisite architecture & the breathtaking splendour of Punakha Dzong.
Hike to Tiger’s Nest (Taktsang) Monastery in Paro, perched 10,240 ft high on a cliff, where legend says Guru Rinpoche flew on a tigress’ back.
Stand before the majestic 177-ft Buddha Dordenma in Thimphu, enjoying stunning views of Thimphu Valley’s green hills and city skyline.
Feast your eyes on the unparalleled views from Dochula Pass, showcasing 108 chortens and Mt. Gangkhar Puensum, the world’s tallest unclimbed peak at 24,836 ft.
Explore Gangtey Monastery, renowned for its ancient architecture and stunning views of the Phobjikha Valley, home to the rare Black-Necked Cranes.
inclusions: 2 nights stay in Phuntsholing with breakfast and lunch or dinner
2 nights stay in Thimphu City with breakfast and lunch or dinner
2 nights stay in Punakha with breakfast and lunch or dinner
2 nights stay in Paro with breakfast and lunch or dinner

know_before_you_go: Images are for representation purpose only.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: Upon your arrival in Siliguri, you'll be transferred to Phuntsholing, a scenic border town of Bhutan. Once you check in to your hotel, enjoy the rest of the day at leisure. You can explore various attractions such as Zangto Pelri, a peaceful monastery with stunning views, Bhutan Gate, an iconic entryway showcasing Bhutanese architecture, and the Amo Chhu Crocodile Breeding Center, home to rare species. In the evening, you can enjoy a relaxing stroll along the Torsa River.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: In the morning, check out and visit the immigration office to secure your travel permit before continuing your journey to Thimphu. En route, stop by Chukha Dam, a key hydroelectric project in Bhutan. Upon arrival in Thimphu, check in and relax. Later, you can explore the city's attractions on your own. You can visit the Royal Botanical Garden, which showcases Bhutan’s diverse plant species, or take a stroll through the peaceful Ludrong Memorial Garden.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, get driven for Thimphu sightseeing tour. Visit various sites such as National Memorial Chorten, Changangkha Lhakhang, Simply Bhutan Museum and many more. Continue to the Motithang Takin Preserve, home to the rare takin, Bhutan’s national animal. Next, explore the Tashichho Dzong, a historical fortress that houses several temples and shrines. Also, explore the Royal Textile Museum & discover Bhutan’s artistic heritage. After the tour, you’ll be driven back to the hotel.

days.title: Transfer to Punakha via Dochula Pass
days.desc: After checking out, get driven to Punakha, with a scenic stop at Dochula Pass to take in panoramic views of the snow-capped Himalayas. Next, visit Chimi Lhakhang, the "Temple of Fertility," built in 1499. Its most striking feature is the golden roof, gleaming in sunlight, with rows of prayer wheels. Continue to Punakha Dzong, a majestic fortress which once served as the seat of the government. End your tour at Punakha Suspension bridge & later, check in to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Day Trip to Gangtey
days.desc: Today, you'll be driven to Gangtey on a day trip. Begin by visiting the Phobjikha Valley, a stunning glacial valley famous for its role as the winter habitat of the endangered black-necked cranes. Enjoy the breathtaking natural scenery and learn about the valley’s ecological significance. Next, explore the historic Gangtey Monastery, a 17th-century Nyingmapa monastery perched on a hill, offering spectacular views of the surrounding landscape. Afterward, get driven back to your hotel in Punakha.

days.title: Transfer to Paro | Paro Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Post check out, get driven to Paro. Upon arrival, enjoy a sightseeing tour, starting with a visit to the Rinpung Dzong, a majestic monastery showcasing traditional Bhutanese architecture. Continue to the National Museum of Bhutan, housed in a historic watchtower, and delve into the country's rich cultural heritage. Later, take a leisurely stroll across the Nyamai Zam wooden bridge, offering scenic views of the Paro River. Afterward, check in to your hotel for an overnight stay.

days.title: Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
days.desc: Begin your day by getting driven to the base of Tiger’s Nest. Then, embark on a scenic 7-km hike through serene pine forests adorned with colorful prayer flags. Along the way, enjoy breathtaking views of the Paro Valley as you approach the monastery, dramatically perched on a rugged cliff. Inside, discover ancient relics, meditation chambers, and stunning murals honoring Guru Rinpoche, a revered figure in Bhutanese Buddhism. After the descent, get driven back to your hotel.

days.title: Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: Today, check out and get driven to Phuntsholing, with a scenic stop at Chele La Pass, the highest motorable pass in Bhutan. Take in the panoramic views of the Himalayan peaks and vibrant prayer flags fluttering against the backdrop of lush valleys. Upon reaching Phuntsholing, check in at your hotel and enjoy the day at leisure. Later, you can visit the Karbandi Monastery, which offers breathtaking views of the town or explore the Phuentsholing Market, known for its local crafts and produce.
